Bug_Title: TQ: Value without a type qualifier used where a value is required to have that qualifier (TQ_UNKNOWN_VALUE_USED_WHERE_ALWAYS_STRICTLY_REQUIRED)
Bug_Details:
A value is being used in a way that requires the value to be annotated with a type qualifier.
The type qualifier is strict, so the tool rejects any values that do not have
the appropriate annotation.
     
    To coerce a value to have a strict annotation, define an identity function where the return value is annotated
with the strict annotation.
This is the only way to turn a non-annotated value into a value with a strict type qualifier annotation.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is created by accessing an array index out of its bounds. Java does not throw an error when trying to access an index that exceeds the array's length, instead it returns the default value for the array type. In this case, it returns 0, which is an int.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case fails because it triggers the bug. The bug is caused by trying to access an index that exceeds the length of the array 'values', which results in returning the default value for the array type, which is 0.
